newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end firm after intra-day yr high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end firm after intra-day yr high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended firm on Monday, after the Hang Seng index hit a new 1996 intra-day high, with investors hoping that if the U.S. Federal Reserve raises interest rates this week, it will only be a small hike.

"There seem to be no concerns over the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting. Most people have discounted a 25 basis point rise so they think that should be enough for the time being," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities (HK) Ltd.
The Hang Seng index closed the session 29.77 points higher at 11,622.13, after hitting a year high at 11,684.00.
Turnover was HK$4.86 billion compared to HK$5.15 billion on Friday.
Edward Chan, research director at NAVA SC Securities, said fundamentals should carry the index to even higher levels and he expected the Hang Seng to reach 12,200 points by the end of the year.
"As long as rates don't go up by a significant amount, I think most investors have discounted the rise and people will focus on the fundamentals," he said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve policy-setting body meets on Tuesday.
Chan said investors were particularly optimistic about the property sector due to the enthusiastic reponse to recent property development sales.
"The main feature of the market is still property," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Henderson Land hit a new all-time high on Monday at HK$66.50 and ended the session up HK$1.75 at a record close of HK$66.25.

Hysan Development rose HK$0.30 to HK$23.95. It reported interim net profit of HK$697.45 million compared to HK$632.28 million. Amoy Properties fell HK$0.15 to HK$8.95. Analysts said its 1995/96 net profit of HK$1.58 billion was disappointing.
HSBC Holdings also hit a record intra-day high at HK$143.00 before closing the session up HK$0.50 at HK$142.00.
Hongkong Ferry jumped HK$2.30 to HK$14.30 on hopes of strong earnings from the redevelopment of its old shipyard site at Tai Kok Tsui into a comprehensive complex.

COSCO Pacific closed down HK$0.35 at HK$6.55 after running up on Friday ahead of the issue of warrants by three merchant banks. The company posted interim net profit of HK$32.40 million compared with HK$21.98 million. South China Morning Post reported net profit of HK$695.87 million compared with HK$580.06 million. The stock closed on a gain of HK$0.10 at HK$5.40.
